confidenceLimiters.text: The OpenSpec delta spec carries a scenario — 'Filtering by a priority that matches no task' — with no automated test. The seeded singleton store always holds at least one task of every priority, and changing the seed is outside the approved scope, so the empty-result path cannot be exercised over HTTP without making the suite order-dependent. Covered by inspection only; see the C-001 whyNotTest.

The T0 (mechanical-tier) implementation of this unit was verified and REJECTED at post-condition review: it accepted `?priority=Low,High` with a 200. The unit was escalated T0 -> T1 (1 of 2 budget spent) and redone at ceiling under the overhead guard. The delivered code is the redone version; a regression test pins the defect.

`chaos-record`'s build/test log parser produced empty facts against this machine's Spanish-locale dotnet output ('0 Advertencia(s)', '0 Errores', 'Superado: 42'). The values recorded here are the observed results of the runs whose logs were passed to the emitter, not estimates. Todo candidate: make the parser locale-tolerant.

verdictRationale: Every contract statement is delivered and covered, build and tests are green (42/42, up from a 34-test baseline), the diff never left the approved scope, and both material decisions are answered, consumed and recorded. The one non-test coverage row (C-006) is structural and carries its whyNotTest.
commentary: The substantive engineering finding of this run is RK-1 turning out to be wider than framed. The frame anticipated that `Enum.TryParse` accepts numeric strings; it also ORs comma-separated names together for enums that are not [Flags], so `?priority=Low,High` parses to `High` (0|2) and `Enum.IsDefined` then confirms it as declared. A digit-prefix guard plus `Enum.IsDefined` — the T0 implementation — passes every test that was asked for and still violates C-003. The delivered code matches the declared names explicitly instead, which closes the whole class rather than the two instances that had tests. Note this also fixes repeated parameters for free: `?priority=High&priority=Low` binds as the single string 'High,Low' and is now correctly a 400.

coverage.whyNotTest: Partially. The matching/ordering half is tested directly. The delta spec's 'recognised priority that matches no task -> 200 + empty array' scenario is NOT tested: the seeded singleton store always holds a task of every priority, and reseeding or deleting to create the empty case would either leave the approved scope or make the suite order-dependent. That branch is covered by inspection — the handler returns Results.Ok on the filtered list unconditionally, so an empty match yields 200 with [] and cannot yield 404.

deviations.summary: M5 scope-spill fired at the first K3 rescan against the K1 scope string. The delivered diff never left the approved scope — the scope had been supplied as annotated prose the scan's path matcher does not read as a path list. Confirmed by the human, then re-baselined to a plain path list via `scan.py update-scope`; the trigger itself stays fired (the classifier is monotone).
